For each moving subject describe trajectory both relative to the main subject (passing to her right, approaching from behind, moving alongside) and relative to the camera (toward/away from the camera, to the left/right edge of the frame). For every visible person specify head orientation and precise gaze direction using clear phrases (for example, "looking directly at the camera," "eyes down at the phone," "gaze directed up and to the left," "looking toward the car"); do this for all people in the scene. When people interact, report only observable interaction cues and roles—describe who is addressing or reacting to whom using visible evidence (open mouth facing another as an indicator of speaking; turned body, raised hand or pointing as gestures; facing and still with closed mouth as listening or observing) rather than inference. For interactions with objects or structures state exactly how a subject is using them (holding, gripping, resting, pulling, supporting, leaning on), which hand and side (left/right), and whether the hand is in contact, gripping, merely near, or in motion versus resting. Describe body posture with concrete camera‑relative terms (standing, weight shifted onto left/right leg, slightly leaning forward/back, seated, reclining, crouching, mid‑jump, arms outstretched, knees bent) and specify orientation to the camera (facing the camera, in profile, back to the camera). Clarify precise spatial relationships, counts, arrangement, proximity and scale using camera‑relative language and clear phrases (foreground/midground/background; left/middle/right of frame; across the foreground of; directly in front of/behind; a few feet/meters apart; clustered closely; in a line or scattered). Describe lighting, shadows and visible surface textures with observable cues and an approximate shadow direction or length (for example, "bright direct sunlight casting long shadows toward the lower left," "diffuse overcast," "wet pavement reflecting light"); note absence of distinct shadows when apparent. Report facial expressions or visible affect only when clearly evident using observable detail (open‑mouthed, smiling with teeth visible, furrowed brow). Keep the caption concise, factual and single‑sentence. Output exactly one single sentence.
